questions.q: What controls a managed table's storage location?
options: Unity Catalog fully controls it — you never specify it, and it's chosen under the catalog's MANAGED LOCATION
The user must always specify an exact LOCATION for a managed table
Managed tables don't have a storage location at all
The Databricks Runtime version determines the location
questions.explain: This lets Unity Catalog guarantee things about the table's full lifecycle, including cleanup on drop.

questions.q: What does Unity Catalog manage for an external table, versus what it doesn't?
options: It manages the table's metadata (schema, registration, permissions) but not the underlying files' lifecycle
It manages everything exactly the same as a managed table
It manages the files' lifecycle but not the metadata
External tables have no metadata management at all
questions.explain: An external table points at a location you specify — often data other tools outside Databricks also need to read.

questions.q: What actually happens when you DROP a managed table versus an external table?
options: Dropping a managed table deletes both the metadata AND the underlying data files; dropping an external table only removes the registration, leaving the files untouched
Both operations behave identically, deleting only the metadata
Both operations delete the underlying files regardless of table type
Dropping an external table always fails with an error
questions.explain: Confusing these two is a real, common way to either destroy data accidentally or leave orphaned files behind.

questions.q: Why is a managed table a good fit for this course's bronze/silver/gold tables?
options: Unity Catalog fully owns their lifecycle, from creation through VACUUM and eventual deletion, with no external tool needing direct file access
Managed tables are always faster to query than external ones
External tables cannot be queried using SQL
Managed tables don't support MERGE or UPDATE operations
questions.explain: External tables are the right choice specifically when something outside Databricks needs direct file access.

questions.q: What real mistake can happen from confusing managed and external tables?
options: Accidentally destroying data by dropping a managed table thinking it's external, or leaving orphaned files by dropping an external table expecting cleanup
There's no real risk; both types behave identically on DROP
Only a performance slowdown, never actual data loss
A schema mismatch error, but no data loss
questions.explain: This is exactly the practical risk of not understanding the DROP TABLE distinction between the two types.
